attempted_claim: Let X/Q be a K3 surface of degree 2 and geometric Picard rank 1 arising from the Hassett-Varilly-Alvarado construction from a smooth cubic fourfold containing a plane, i.e. w^2 = -1/2 det [[2A,B,C],[B,2D,E],[C,E,2F]] with A,...,F homogeneous quadrics, equipped with its canonical 2-torsion transcendental class alpha in Br(X) given by (B^2-4AD,A), and with X(A_Q) nonempty. Decide: does X(A_Q)^{Br(X)} nonempty imply X(Q) nonempty? Equivalently, does there exist such an X with X(A_Q) nonempty, X(A_Q)^{Br(X)} nonempty, but X(Q) empty, requiring a beyond-Brauer-Manin explanation?
decisive_failure: No TARGET, preset, or emergent claim is made. Local-solubility evidence is heuristic (real sampling, mod-p branch counts, no p-adic lifting proof); bounded-box point absence never certifies rational-point emptiness; Hilbert-symbol and smoothness routines are standard methods only. All scripts are exploratory working notes, not verification of any theorem.
